channel.title: daryo
channel.description: Regional headlines in English, updated four times a day.

item.title: Uzbekistan Reforms Liquefied Gas Supply System Amidst Shortages
item.description: Uzbekistan's President Mirziyoyev reviewed proposals to reform the liquefied gas supply system. The system currently faces issues with timely delivery, affecting 3.8 million people and 2,000 social facilities. 22 percent of consumers experience delays exceeding 46 days, leading to higher costs.

item.title: Uzbekistan and Serbia Elevate Relations from Political Dialogue to Practical Partnership
item.description: Uzbekistan's President Mirziyoyev will visit Serbia on September 7-8 to strengthen bilateral ties. Recent years have seen increased political dialogue and economic contacts. The visit aims to transform political trust into concrete economic results, including trade, investment, and cooperation.

item.title: Uzbekistan Cancels 1.3 Billion Som Unjustified Tax Debt for Citizen
item.description: Uzbekistan's justice authorities canceled an unjustified tax debt of over 1.3 billion som for a citizen in Mubarek district. The debt was incorrectly levied on land the citizen did not use. The Kashkadarya regional justice department intervened after the citizen appealed, leading to the annulment of the charge.

item.title: Two killed in Surxondaryo after car collides with train at unguarded crossing
item.description: Two women, aged 47 and 30, died when a Gentra car collided with a train at an unguarded railway crossing in Denov district, Surxondaryo region. The accident occurred due to driver negligence. A two-year-old girl and the driver were injured and hospitalized.

item.title: Prosecution seeks nine-year sentences in 'Letter of 75' appeal case
item.description: Prosecutors are requesting nine-year prison sentences for all defendants in the 'Letter of 75' case appeal at the Bishkek City Court. This follows a previous verdict where defendants were found guilty of violent seizure of power and received four-year sentences with probation.

item.title: New Traffic Safety Powers for PPX, Traffic Police to Aid Public Order from November 2026
item.description: The PPX (Public Patrol Service) will be granted new powers related to traffic safety. Additionally, traffic police officers will assume certain functions and powers for maintaining public order starting from November 1, 2026. Further details are available via the provided link.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan Considers Bill to Allow Existing Homes Near Issyk-Kul Shoreline
item.description: A bill introduced in Kyrgyzstan's Jogorku Kenesh proposes to amend regulations for houses located within 500 meters of Issyk-Kul's shoreline. The amendment aims to allow existing individual residential buildings, constructed before August 2004 with valid land documents, to remain, addressing legal uncertainties for owners.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan Proposes Expedited Trademark Registration Process
item.description: Kyrgyzstan is considering a bill to reform trademark, geographical indication, and place of origin registration. Key changes include introducing an accelerated examination option for trademarks upon payment of a fee, aiming for a four-month processing time. The bill also addresses digitalization and regional brands.

item.title: Prosecution Seeks Nine-Year Sentence in 'Letter of 75' Case Appeal
item.description: In Bishkek, the prosecution is seeking a nine-year prison sentence for all defendants in the appeal of the 'Letter of 75' case, which concerns alleged preparation for a violent seizure of power. Previously, a lower court sentenced the defendants to four years with a three-year probation period, a decision appealed by both the prosecution and the accused.

item.title: Uzbek President Discusses Customs Cooperation with World Customs Organization Secretary General
item.description: Uzbek President Shavkat Mirziyoyev met with the Secretary General of the World Customs Organization. They discussed expanding practical cooperation in improving customs administration, strengthening customs authorities' capabilities, and combating offenses.

item.title: Nepal Mourns Over 1,300 Victims of Devastating River Flood
item.description: Nepal is observing a day of mourning for over 1,300 victims of a river flood in the Bhote-Koshi River. The disaster left 32,000 families homeless, destroyed nearly 7,500 homes, and caused significant infrastructure damage. Around 5,000 people, including 589 foreigners, are missing.

item.title: Tursunzade Farmers Supply Over 70,000 Tons of Agricultural Products to Tajikistan
item.description: Farmers in Tursunzade have supplied 70,565 tons of agricultural products to markets across Tajikistan, including Dushanbe and the Sughd region. This includes significant quantities of potatoes, onions, cabbage, tomatoes, cucumbers, carrots, grapes, fruits, and dairy products.

item.title: Uzbekistan Appoints Ambassador to Syria, Ayubkhon Yunusov
item.description: Uzbekistan has appointed Ayubkhon Yunusov as its ambassador to Syria. Yunusov also concurrently serves as Uzbekistan's ambassador to Kuwait and Iraq. The appointment signifies an expansion of diplomatic representation in the region.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan's Tax Service to Integrate Artificial Intelligence with Expert Help
item.description: Kyrgyzstan's State Tax Service (STS) met with Sign, a digital infrastructure developer, to discuss integrating AI into tax administration. The collaboration aims to modernize digital infrastructure, enhance analytical systems, and develop domestic IT capabilities. Both parties expressed readiness for joint initiatives in digital transformation.

item.title: New Electric Train Service Launched Between Parkent and Tashkent
item.description: An electric train service has been launched connecting Parkent and Tashkent, reducing travel time to approximately 50 minutes. Ticket prices are set at 10,000 Uzbek soums for adults and 6,500 soums for children under 10.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan's Tax Service to Integrate Artificial Intelligence with Expert Help
item.description: Kyrgyzstan's State Tax Service (STS) met with Sign, a digital infrastructure developer, to discuss integrating AI into tax administration. The collaboration aims to modernize digital infrastructure, enhance analytical systems, and develop domestic IT capabilities. Both parties expressed readiness for joint initiatives in digital transformation.

item.title: Uzbekistan Among Countries Selling Gold in July
item.description: In July 2026, the Central Bank of Uzbekistan sold one ton of gold, joining other central banks that reduced their reserves. China was the largest buyer, acquiring 20 tons, while Poland purchased 8 tons. Russia sold 6 tons. Globally, central banks bought approximately 130 tons of gold in the first seven months of 2026.

item.title: Astana to Host AI & Digital Bridge 2026 Forum
item.description: Astana will host the AI & Digital Bridge 2026 forum from October 1-3, focusing on artificial intelligence's impact on markets and business. The event aims to connect global BigTech, investors, and partners, and showcase AI solutions. Kazakhstan declared 2026 the Year of Digitalization and AI, underscoring the forum's strategic importance.

item.title: Uzbek President Receives Chinese Delegation
item.description: Uzbek President Shavkat Mirziyoyev met with a Chinese delegation led by Liu Haixin, head of the International Liaison Department of the CPC Central Committee. They discussed expanding multifaceted cooperation and practical partnerships between Uzbekistan and China.

item.title: Polat Bobojonov Appointed First Deputy Chairman of Uzbekistan Mahalla Association
item.description: Polat Bobojonov has been appointed First Deputy Chairman of the Uzbekistan Mahalla Association. This follows his dismissal from the position of Deputy Advisor to the President on personnel matters, a role and department that have now been abolished.

item.title: Tajikistan, Russia, Kazakhstan, Kyrgyzstan Inspect Arms Control Compliance in China
item.description: Military personnel from Tajikistan, Russia, Kazakhstan, and Kyrgyzstan conducted an arms control inspection in China's Heilongjiang province on September 7, 2026. The inspection verified compliance with disarmament agreements in the border region, with no violations found by the Chinese Ministry of Defense.

item.title: Farg'ona Governorate and Afghanistan's Kam Air Discuss Establishing New International Airline
item.description: The Farg'ona Governorate and Afghanistan's Kam Air are discussing the establishment of a new international airline. Discussions followed a July visit to Afghanistan where agreements on trade, economic, and investment cooperation were reached. Details on launch dates and investment volumes remain unclarified.

item.title: Number of emigrants from Uzbekistan decreased in first half of 2026
item.description: The number of citizens emigrating from Uzbekistan has decreased. Data indicates the primary destination countries for those who did leave during the first half of 2026.

item.title: CIS intelligence chiefs discuss cooperation in intelligence gathering
item.description: Heads of security and intelligence services from CIS countries met in St. Petersburg on September 4, 2026, to discuss cooperation in intelligence activities. Russian President Vladimir Putin emphasized the importance of this interaction for strengthening sovereignty and security within the CIS.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan's Labor Minister Kanat Sagynbaev Dismissed; Almaz Imangaziev Appointed Acting Head
item.description: Kanat Sagynbaev has been dismissed as Kyrgyzstan's Minister of Labor, Social Security, and Migration. Almaz Imangaziev has been appointed acting minister. Imangaziev, a professional diplomat, previously served as Deputy Foreign Minister and headed the Consular Service Department.

item.title: Tender Announced for Reconstruction of Bridge Over Aravan-Ak-Buura Canal in Osh
item.description: Osh, Kyrgyzstan, has announced a tender for the reconstruction of the bridge over the Aravan-Ak-Buura canal. The project, managed by 'Osh City Roads' Municipal Enterprise, has a budget of 37.4 million soms. The reconstruction involves demolishing existing structures and building a new reinforced concrete bridge.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan proposes prison for intentional damage to border fences
item.description: Kyrgyzstan has submitted a bill proposing criminal liability for intentionally damaging state border infrastructure. The draft law suggests two to five years in prison for damaging engineering structures and barriers, citing a lack of specific provisions and the risk of unauthorized crossings. Over 320 km of barriers are installed on the Kyrgyz-Tajik border.

item.title: Iran warns US of harsher response amid renewed military tensions
item.description: Iran's leadership has warned the United States of a more painful response as military confrontations between Tehran and Washington intensify. Parliament Speaker Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf urged the US to properly assess the situation. The warning comes amid renewed military tensions between the two countries.

item.title: Almaz Imangaziev Appointed Acting Labor Minister of Kyrgyzstan
item.description: Kanat Sagynbaev has been dismissed as Kyrgyzstan's Minister of Labor, Social Security, and Migration. Almaz Imangaziev, previously Deputy Foreign Minister, is now acting head of the ministry. His appointment requires approval from the Zhogorku Kenesh. Imangaziev is a career diplomat with a PhD in political science.

item.title: Almaz Imangaziev Appointed Acting Labor Minister of Kyrgyzstan
item.description: Kanat Sagynbaev has been dismissed as Kyrgyzstan's Minister of Labor, Social Security, and Migration. Almaz Imangaziev, previously Deputy Foreign Minister, is now acting head of the ministry. His appointment requires approval from the Zhogorku Kenesh. Imangaziev is a career diplomat with a PhD in political science.

item.title: Gazprom Increases Gas Exports to Central Asia by 70 Percent
item.description: Gazprom has increased its gas exports to Central Asia by 70 percent since the beginning of 2026, according to company head Alexey Miller. Deliveries to Kazakhstan, Uzbekistan, and Kyrgyzstan are nearing this growth mark. Kyrgyzstan requires nearly half a billion cubic meters of gas annually.

item.title: G'ofurjon Mirzayev appointed Deputy Prime Minister and Chairman of Mahalla Association
item.description: G'ofurjon Mirzayev has been appointed Deputy Prime Minister and Chairman of the Association of Mahallas of Uzbekistan. His candidacy was approved by deputies of the Legislative Chamber of the Oliy Majlis. Mirzayev replaces Kahramon Kurbonov, who held the position since January 17, 2024.

item.title: Gazprom boosts Central Asian gas exports by 70 percent
item.description: Gazprom CEO Alexey Miller announced a 70 percent increase in gas exports to Central Asia since the start of 2026. Supplies to Kazakhstan, Uzbekistan, and Kyrgyzstan have approached this mark. Long-term agreements are in place through 2040 for Kyrgyzstan's energy facilities.

item.title: New oil processing line construction begins in Jayhun district
item.description: Construction of a new oil processing line with a capacity of 50,000 tons of petroleum products per year has commenced in the Jayhun district. The Ministry of Energy and Water Resources of Tajikistan reported that the new line will enable the production of diesel fuel and gasoline, expanding the product range beyond bitumen.

item.title: New powers for traffic police and public order units in Uzbekistan
item.description: Uzbekistan is reallocating functions between internal affairs units to enhance public safety. From November 1, 2026, patrol units will respond to crimes and incidents via the '112' system. Patrol units will also gain new responsibilities for traffic safety, including managing congestion in busy areas.

item.title: Uzbek Citizen Sentenced to Two Years for Fighting in Ukraine
item.description: An Uzbek citizen, F.A., who fought for Russia in the Ukraine conflict, has been sentenced to two years in prison in Namangan, Uzbekistan. He was recruited while serving a drug sentence in Russia and participated in combat operations before being injured by a drone strike. He later returned to Uzbekistan and obtained citizenship.

item.title: Uzbek Preventive Police Officers Granted Authority to Issue Fines for Traffic Violations
item.description: Preventive police officers in Uzbekistan have been granted new powers to issue administrative fines for four types of traffic violations on neighborhood streets. This is part of a presidential decree aimed at improving public safety and community engagement. Officers can now also issue warnings for minor offenses.

item.title: Man Arrested for Assault and Threatening to Kill a Cafeteria Worker in Tajikistan
item.description: Authorities in Tajikistan have arrested a man, Nurmurodzoda Zakhriddin, for assaulting and threatening to kill a cafeteria worker in Zafarabad district. The incident occurred on August 19, 2026, when the intoxicated man reportedly argued with and physically attacked the employee, using a cord to threaten her life.

item.title: Ayubkhon Yunusov Becomes Uzbekistan's First Ambassador to Syria
item.description: Ayubkhon Yunusov presented his credentials as Uzbekistan's first ambassador to Syria to Foreign Minister Asad Hasan ash-Shayboni. The meeting focused on strengthening bilateral ties, including establishing a joint trade and economic committee and political consultations. Both sides expressed readiness for further cooperation.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan to Export Berries and Fruits to China Following Phytosanitary Protocol Signing
item.description: Kyrgyzstan will export berries and fruits, including raspberries, blackberries, and currants, to China. A phytosanitary protocol was signed within the Shanghai Cooperation Organization framework, expanding export opportunities beyond traditional EAEU markets and potentially boosting domestic berry cultivation.
